newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares power ahead to close at new high.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares power ahead to close at new high.

text.p: Italian shares powered ahead to a new high on Friday, driven by a tidal wave of lquidity as domestic investors switched funds from bonds into equities, with Fiat leading the way with an 8.71 percent leap in value.
The all-share mibtel index finished 2.87 percent higher at 11,418 while the mib30 index ended the session 3.3 percent up at 17,136.

The biggest gains were made by stocks that lagged behind the main pack in the closing weeks of 1996. "Everything of any quality that got left behind has been heavily bought," said David Roberts, an equities specialist at CIMO in Milan.

Fiat, which finished at 4,816 lire, was boosted by a rush of buying spurred by an increase in car registrations in December, signalling that Italy's languishing car market could be poised for a recovery.
Investors appeared to completely shrug off an announcement by Fiat late on Thursday that it was recalling 80,000 Fiat Bravo/Brava models to replace a brake component.
"In a normal market the Fiat recall might have had an impact but it's true that most volume car producers have to do this sometimes," said a Milan-based stockbroker.
Regular favourites with foreign investors such as ENI, which finished 3.84 percent higher at 8,644 lire were left standing by star performers led by insurance stocks Generali and Alleanza.
Generali ended 5.87 percent up at 31,683 lire with Alleanza closing 4.68 percent higher at 11,389 lire.
Lower quality stocks also attracted attention. "In a liquidity-driven market it is often better to go for lower quality shares because they are rising from a lower level," said Roberts.
Fochi Spa, a troubled engineering firm, shot up by 28.86 percent to close at 192 lire in fairly thin volume.
